atoms.text: The clone who meets himself: a solitary worker discovers his own duplicate, so the protagonist's uniqueness — the basis of his identity — is revealed as consumable.
Clones with implanted memories: each copy believes he is the original with a family waiting on Earth, so hope is a manufactured incentive.
The three-year contract as lifespan: clones are activated for a fixed term and disposed of when they degrade, so employment is literally a death sentence.
The AI caretaker who chooses sides: a helper robot follows corporate orders until it quietly helps the clones, so obedience is a dial rather than a switch.
The value of a life measured in output: the company treats each clone as a replaceable unit, so the story asks what a person is worth beyond productivity.
The forbidden live call: a communications blackout is revealed as deliberate isolation, so the protagonist's loneliness is policy rather than accident.
Two versions of the same man: older and newer clones cooperate and compete, so selfhood becomes a negotiation between copies with different remaining time.
The hidden vault of sleeping clones: a room full of identical bodies turns a personal mystery into an industrial inventory.
Memories as leased property: the clones' families are real memories belonging to another man, so love is genuine in the copy and stolen from the original.
The far side of the Moon: isolation is geographical and total, so the setting enforces the theme of being out of sight and out of mind.
The dying clone's escape plan: a copy near death helps his successor escape, so solidarity across replacements becomes a form of inheritance.
Helium-3 as the world's fuel: one worker sustains an energy economy, so the protagonist's solitude is the hidden cost of civilization's comfort.
Recorded messages from home: family videos are the only connection to Earth, so intimacy is mediated by a one-way archive.
The crash that starts the countdown: an accident reveals the replacement protocol, so the plot's inciting incident is the system's maintenance routine.
The right to know you are a copy: the clones' ignorance is engineered, so dignity is defined as access to the truth about one's own origin.
The AI as witness and accomplice: the caretaker knows the whole truth and reveals it slowly, so care and complicity are performed in the same voice.
